Description

Normal Deformation as Constrained Refoliation is the third paper in the Wheeler–DeWitt ARC. It establishes the normal-deformation and refoliation structure required for the representation-stable canonical gravity realization obtained through WDW‑1 and WDW‑2.

Its central question is:



When an authenticated Einstein–source realization is presented on different admissible hypersurfaces, under what conditions does normal deformation preserve one constrained physical realization rather than generate a slicing-dependent replacement?


The manuscript treats normal deformation as a constrained refoliation problem. Building on the connection-typed canonical projection of WDW‑1 and the proper-redescription groupoid descent of WDW‑2, it develops the lapse-directed normal and shift-directed tangential deformation roles together with the constraint relations required for their lawful composition.

Description

Configuration-Space Differentiation and the Constraint-Native Wheeler–DeWitt Candidate Family is the fifth paper in the Wheeler–DeWitt ARC. It carries the source-attached, jointly constrained classical interior established by WDW‑4 across the next type boundary: to separately typed, regulator-indexed quantum-constraint candidate families.

Its central question is:



Given the completed WDW‑4 classical gravity–matter constraint interior, what configuration carriers, differential structures, representations, and constraint actions can be constructed without silently claiming quantum closure that has not yet been earned?


The manuscript constructs two distinct branches:





a metric–scalar/clock core; and




a torsion-free tetrad–Standard-Model extension incorporating spin, gauge, Higgs, and chiral-fermion structure.



For each branch, it supplies local Sobolev configuration carriers; proper-redescription action and local descent; tangent, cotangent, and canonical normalization data; separating test algebras; independently defined first and second Fréchet differentials; regulated Hessian contractions; algebraic CCR/CAR representation seeds; and complete linear and Hamiltonian constraint actions on one algebraically invariant test domain.

Its central passage is:

[\text{joint WDW-4 classical constraint interior}\longrightarrow\text{configuration-space differentiation and regulated representations}\longrightarrow\text{constraint-native Wheeler--DeWitt candidate families}.]

The paper does not insert a formal Wheeler–DeWitt expression as a primitive. Coincident second-order functional contractions are replaced by declared positive-regulator traces, and the resulting constraint families are classified within their stated compatibility class. Formal joint solutions are considered only in the algebraic dual, with no claim that this already provides a physical state space.

The endpoint is deliberately exact: WDW‑5 reaches the regulator-indexed algebraic candidate level. Those are the expressly exported burdens of WDW‑6.

Description

Complete Joint Constraint-Kernel Realization Closure for the Wheeler–DeWitt System is the ninth paper in the Wheeler–DeWitt ARC. It brings the preceding canonical, quantum, temporal, covariant–canonical, and controlled semiclassical results into one jointly realized Wheeler–DeWitt constraint kernel.

Its central question is:



Given the surviving Wheeler–DeWitt realization, its admissible profile-clock structure, and its controlled covariant–canonical and semiclassical recoveries, what joint constraint kernel must be realized for the system to count as a complete physical realization rather than a collection of separately compatible constructions?


The manuscript closes the relevant constraint roles together: the descended canonical gravity structure, refoliation conditions, integrated gravity–matter occupancy, differentiated quantum candidate data, renormalized quantum survival, and the qualified relational and semiclassical structures inherited from WDW‑7 and WDW‑8. The endpoint is not a formal conjunction of independently asserted conditions, but a jointly constrained realization in which the required roles coexist without loss of provenance, standing, or constraint compatibility.

Its central passage is:

[\text{controlled Wheeler--DeWitt realization}\longrightarrow\text{joint constraint-kernel closure}\longrightarrow\text{complete physical realization of the Wheeler--DeWitt system}.]

The paper distinguishes the standing-bearing joint kernel from presentation-dependent representatives: a chosen foliation, clock profile, canonical chart, covariant presentation, semiclassical branch, or local solution form may support an admissible presentation, but cannot replace the jointly realized constraint system itself.

WDW‑9 therefore does not treat a formal state satisfying one operator equation as sufficient for physical realization. Complete closure requires compatibility across the inherited gravitational, matter, redescription, refoliation, quantum-survival, and relational roles. The result supplies the completed joint-kernel input for the final global stage.
